Sea state at North Rankin and Goodwyn: wave height exceedance by month

North Rankin and Goodwyn lies on the North West Shelf of Australia at 19.58° S, 116.13° E. Significant wave height there exceeds 2 m about 17% of the time across the whole year, roughly 5 days a month on average. The roughest month is June, with a mean significant wave height of 1.8 m and seas above 2 m about 34% of the time; the calmest is March, with a mean of 1.3 m and about 7.7% of the time above 2 m. Waves above 4 m occur about 0.2% of the time.

Wind at 10 m across the year: typically 5.9 m/s (11 kn), top 10% above 9.6 m/s (19 kn). Monthly means run from 4.9 m/s in March to 6.7 m/s in June.

Weather windows: a typical year gives about 47 spells of 24 h or more with significant wave height below 2 m. The sea is below 2 m about 83% of the time. A calm running past 240 h is counted once per 240 h.

Nearest mapped asset to the data point: Persephone (field (oil and gas), ~132 m water), 13 km away.

Data basis

Data basis: ERA5 reanalysis (ECMWF / Copernicus C3S), 2010-2024, 3 hourly. Data point 19.50° S, 116.00° E (0.5° grid), 16 km from the named position, 43,832 samples. Values are for the nearest grid cell and are not interpolated.

Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information [2010-2024]. ERA5 hourly data on single levels (significant height of combined wind waves and swell). Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for any use of this information.
